name: Company due diligence
summary: Who a US-listed company is and what it has filed: its SEC identity (CIK and ticker), its latest SEC filings and an encyclopedia summary, plus its domain registration when you give its website. US SEC filers only in this version.

rules: identity comes from the registry step; every later step uses it (legal name, ticker)
a run counts only when at least two verified pearls answered (PM 11-15: per run, not per definition)
filings are the SEC filer's latest, with form and filing date
every statement keeps its source link

notes: v1, PM 11-15 decision: US SEC filers only (scope country US; other inputs get the scope notice and no call). Leads are verified pearls 241601 (encyclopedia.summary), 58997 (sec.filings) and 52559 (domain.lookup) by the 11-15 verify snapshot. registry runs on the ops-approved substitute sec-edgar; gleif-lei waits for v2 (non-US). Every external step runs after the identity step, so an unidentified company costs no pearl call. 11-15 (agent team terms check, reports/necklace-terms-2026-11-15): 58997's terms prohibit our use (free and keyless use is not for a business), so it never runs and the required filings slot is empty until the agent team's own EDGAR agent (sec.gov directly) joins it; until then this necklace stays a candidate and does not go to the gate (the gate check reports the slot as not ready). 11-15 13:5x: the agent team's sec-filings (SEC EDGAR directly, f88e98f3) fills the filings slot behind the prohibited 58997; it is planned until ops approves it as a substitute, and a company without an SEC registration is a normal answer (merged as no_us_sec_filings). 11-16 v2 (PM, after gate round 1 failed: 20/30 with the filings grader fixed): the background step searches the company's name without legal forms (slot.registry.search_name) and keeps only the encyclopedia entries about the registry's company (runner.norm_encyclopedia: ticker, CIK, or a title that is the company's name); an answer about other companies or an empty one is discarded and the next member is asked; when no member has an article about the company the step answers 'No encyclopedia article found' (not_found), which the answer set's wiki_article field makes the right answer for such companies. The step stays required. The last background member is the agent team's sec-company-profile (0ff22150): a profile from SEC EDGAR submissions that says it is from SEC filings, not an encyclopedia article (PM 11-16 condition); planned until ops approves it as a substitute. 11-16 (PM, after sec-company-profile failed the encyclopedia role tasks): the background step also accepts company.profile.v1 (also_contracts); sec-company-profile answers that contract (agent team 53a620cc, input company 'CIK {{slot.registry.cik}}') and is judged on its own company role tasks.
scope_notice: This necklace covers companies that file with the US SEC (country US). For other companies, look up the legal entity by name in the GLEIF LEI search (https://search.gleif.org) or ask our Chat for an agent that covers that country.

input_help.name: The company's name as the SEC lists it, for example Apple Inc.
input_help.country: US. This version covers US SEC filers only.
input_help.domain: Optional. The company's website domain without https://, for example apple.com.

demand: Outside rank 2 (Edgar Tools 269k, Companies House UK 33.4k, OpenRegistry 19.2k visits); our records: company lookups 2 in 30 days (reports/necklace-demand-2026-11-15).
